body:
[A10] Follow-up from #686 (PR #695, merged as `17f62ef6`). #686 conformed four items of the fabric MAAP engine (`hdl/ieee1722/maap/KL_maap.sv`) to IEEE 1722-2016 Annex B. These deviations were recorded in [MAAP_FABRIC.md](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/dev/docs/design/MAAP_FABRIC.md) and left for a decision.

| Id | Deviation | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | compare_MAC is not applied in the rProbe!/PROBE and rDefend!/DEFEND cells | Table B.7 note d, B.3.6.4 |
| M2 | DEFEND sends this station's own range instead of echoing the PROBE's requested_start_address and requested_count | B.3.6.6 |
| M3 | Address generator: 16-bit LFSR folded into the pool, not a generator with period at least 2^32 - 1 seeded from MAC plus real-time clock | B.3.6.1 |
| M4 | **Seed timing:** in the shipping `milan_datapath` integration the LFSR seed is sampled during `axis_resetn`, when MAC_ADDR_LO/HI are still 0, so every shipping station seeds `0xACE1` and the station MAC never enters the draws (R548-2-F1) | B.3.4 NOTE, B.3.6.1 |
| M5 | No PortOperational! input, so a returning link does not re-probe | Table B.7, B.3.5.9 |
| M6 | A PROBE parsed while a frame is on the wire is not defended; a missed fourth PROBE is settled by the prober's ANNOUNCE and compare_MAC, which can move this station | Table B.7, B.3.6.3 |
| M7 | A supplied seed (`seed_valid_i`) is used without a range check, so a block outside the Table B.9 dynamic pool can be claimed | Table B.9, B.4 |
| M8 | Truncated MAAP PDUs (pre-existing; R548-1-S2) | B.2 |

**Acceptance:**
1. Each item is either conformed, with a suite check and a planted defect, or justified by clause in MAAP_FABRIC.md.
2. M4 is fixed in RTL first: the seed is taken when the engine is enabled or the MAC is programmed, and a datapath-level check shows two stations with different MACs drawing different intervals.
3. OOC area and one shipping route stay within the then-current budget; resource records are re-recorded through the recipe.
4. Bench interop with the reference peer is unchanged.

Relates to #686.
